“I have mended many things,” my father says. “I have knit a few tea towels for the kitchen, and I have made a few lamps. I learnt woodworking from my father and built a few doll’s houses.”

When I first began learning to shear, I was concerned that it would affect my music. Would I hurt my fingers chopping wood? Would I develop bad habits lifting heavy things? No. I cannot play the piano any more, but the guitar and the bass are part of my life.

3 Cups Flour

1 tsp Salt

1 Cup Almond Milk
½ Cup Oil

4 Tbs Corn Starch (best method)
4 Tbs Sugar

½ tsp Extract

Glaze
½ to ¾ Cup Maple Syrup
½ Cup Powdered Sugar
½ tsp Vanilla

The camera itself is a simple machine. Yes, some are more complex than others, but for the most part every camera operates the same way.

The 15 essential photography principles that follow have stood the test of time. And in short, they describe what you need to know about your camera, in order to make that camera your creative friend rather than your enemy.

It’s just a camera.

Exposure.
Exposure is one of the most important things a photographer learns. It describes how much light reaches the camera sensor and, accordingly, affects everything you photograph: it’s a combination of three main factors – shutter speed, ISO and aperture.

1. Shutters – shutters control the amount of time the camera sensor is exposed to light. The slower your speed (or the longer your shutter is open), the more the camera sensor is exposed. This means that with slow shutter speeds you can capture images in low light, or use a tripod to capture motion blur. With fast shutter speeds you can capture fast moving objects.<start_of_image>Note: When you change the shutter speed, you also change the amount of light that reaches the sensor and, consequently, how light or dark a photo is.
